messages:
Elaine: FYI hitting weird SSE behavior on Windows sample app — after a quick disconnect/reconnect some chunks arrive out of order and the client parser drops payloads. anyone seen this?
Sam: can you share steps and logs?
Elaine: repro steps: run sampleapp (node 18) on Windows 10 with flaky wifi, trigger a long streaming response (~10s). disconnect network for ~300-600ms, reconnect. Parser prints 'unexpected EOF' and we sometimes see duplicated final token.
Elaine: logs:```
[stream-parser] recv 0x1f2 bytes
[stream-parser] emit event id=abc123 seq=42
[stream-parser] unexpected EOF while waiting for "\n\n"
[stream-parser] reconnecting with Last-Event-ID=abc123
[stream-parser] emit event id=abc123 seq=43  <-- duplicate seq but different payload
```
Sam: do you use lastEventId only, or is there an internal sequence in payload?
Elaine: we resume with Last-Event-ID header only. payloads don't have explicit seq numbers currently (we added seq in a patch for debug though). the parser looks for "\n\n" boundary and emits events; partial CRLFs on Windows seem to confuse it.
Mike: this rings a bell — Windows TCP stack sometimes coalesces/segments differently. when the client reconnects the proxy may replay tail bytes and our resume header causes server to send overlap, so you get duplicate bytes around the boundary, which our boundary detection treats as a brand-new event. leads to out-of-order emission.
Jess: two quick ideas: 1) embed a small monotonic seq field inside each event payload so the client can drop duplicates deterministically, 2) make the parser robust to partial CRLFs by treating any CR/LF combination across chunk edges and normalizing before boundary detection. also consider a short jittered backoff on resume to let upstream flush.
Elaine: good call. i pushed a local change to the node sample parser to normalize CRLF and to check an optional seq in the JSON body before emitting. preliminary results look better on my Windows VM.
Sam: can you paste the change?
Elaine: snippet:```js
// normalize buffer for boundary search
buffer = buffer.replace(/\r\n/g, '\n');
// simple seq dedupe
const evt = JSON.parse(payload);
if (seenSeq.has(evt.seq)) { return; }
seenSeq.add(evt.seq);
emit(evt);
```
Infra-bot: streaming-proxy v2.4.1 rolled out to prod @ 2026-03-12T09:12:03Z
Mike: also check the proxy resume logic — if it accepts Last-Event-ID and replays, it should avoid sending the overlapping suffix. adding idempotent seq in payload is safest.
Elaine: opened PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/3124 with parser normalization + e2e test that simulates chunk-splitting on reconnects.
Devex-bot: PR 3124 opened by elaine in repos/sample-streaming (labels: devex, flaky-streams).
Sam: great. can you add a tiny test that injects a 1-3 byte split in the CRLF boundary and runs on Windows CI? otherwise this might slip.
Elaine: yep will add that. assigning follow-ups: add seqs server-side (jess), patch proxy resume to avoid replay overlap (mike), add Windows e2e (elaine).
Jess: I can spike server seq in the model router tomorrow.
Sam: thanks team — nice triage. please post results back here after CI run :thumbsup:
Elaine: will do, thx!
